The libretto was intricate, demanding a delicate balance of emotions and musical expression that I struggled to achieve at that time. When the performance fell short of my expectations, I was filled with a profound sense of disappointment and self-criticism. However, rather than dwell on the failure, I chose to confront it directly.

I delved into a rigorous study of composition and sought guidance from experienced masters to hone my craft. This experience humbled me, reminding me of the importance of patience, discipline, and continuous growth in the pursuit of musical excellence. It taught me the invaluable lesson that true artistry is not solely about grand ambitions but also about the dedication to refine one's skills with humility and perseverance.

In hindsight, that perceived failure became a stepping stone in my artistic journey, guiding me towards a deeper understanding of my own limitations and pushing me to strive for greater mastery in my compositions.
